title: Strict-local coherent cohomology comparison for algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $Y$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and let $F$ be coherent on $X$. Coherent means quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and, on an affine etale cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, associated to finitely generated modules [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, the geometric stalk of the structure sheaf [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Let $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ be the canonical morphism obtained from the compatible maps $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\to A$ for affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $U$ of $\bar y$. Put $X_A=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}A$, with projections $h:X_A\to X$ and $f_A:X_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $F_A=h^*F$. All module sheaves, tensor pullbacks and direct images are on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; $R^qf_*$ and $H^q$ are computed by injective resolutions in all structure-sheaf module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then $A$ is a Noetherian local ring, $c$ is flat, $X_A$ is locally Noetherian, and $F_A$ is coherent. For every $q\geq0$ there is a canonical $A$-linear isomorphism, natural in $F$,
$$(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_A,F_A).$$
It is the comparison induced by flat base change along $c$ and the closed-geometric-point sections comparison on the strictly henselian local base $\operatorname{Spec}A$; its map from a pointed neighbourhood is the usual cohomological pullback along $X_A\to X\times_Y U$. No properness assumption is imposed on $f$.

The same reduction only needs separated finite type, not properness.

proof.text: Choose a Noetherian affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$ containing the image $y$ of $\bar y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] the ring $A$ and its maps from pointed neighbourhoods are the residue-triple colimit over $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] this is the strict henselization of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and is strictly henselian local, with the specified lift $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\bar y$ over the closed point. The ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian: every ideal is the extension of its contraction to $R$, so generators of that contraction generate the localized ideal. Now [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] gives that $A$ is Noetherian. The canonical $R\to A$ is flat by [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat]. Since $c$ factors through $W$, the affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] proves that $c$ is flat.

proof.text: The definition of finite type makes $f$ quasi-compact; its separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-sfb-space-quasiseparated-test-calculus]. Base change preserves quasi-compactness by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] and quasi-separatedness by the former node, so $f_A$ is qcqs. To check local Noetherianity and coherence, start from the affine etale cover $\{V_i\to X\}$ of the coherence hypothesis, with $\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O)$ Noetherian and $F|_{V_i}$ associated to a finitely generated module $M_i$. The preimage of $W$ in $V_i$ is open; cover it by principal affine opens $V=D(s)\subset V_i$. On each, $F|_V$ is associated to $(M_i)_s$, still finitely generated, and these $V$ are affine etale charts over the fixed affine open $W$ of Step 1 covering $f^{-1}W$. Their maps $V\to W$ are locally of finite type by the chart definition. The base-changed charts $V\times_W\operatorname{Spec}A$ have coordinate rings generated over $A$ by the images of finitely many generators of the coordinate ring of $V$ over that of $W$. They are locally of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; cover each by affine opens with Noetherian coordinate rings, as in the definition of local Noetherianity, and restrict to them. These affine schemes are etale over $X_A$ by base change and cover $X_A=f^{-1}W\times_W\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], $F_A$ is quasi-coherent. On each such chart $F_A$ is associated to the base change of $(M_i)_s$, and then to its restriction to the smaller affine open; finite generating lists tensor to finite generating lists, so $F_A$ is coherent in the stated chartwise sense.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-higher-image-base-change] to $g=c$, using the flatness of Step 1 and the qcqs hypothesis verified in Step 2. For each $q\geq0$ it gives the canonical natural isomorphism $c^*R^qf_*F\simeq R^q(f_A)_*F_A$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] to $f_A$ and $F_A$ to identify $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,R^q(f_A)_*F_A)$ with $H^q(X_A,F_A)$. All hypotheses here are qcqs and quasi-coherence; properness is unnecessary.

Put $N=R^qf_*F$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] to the underlying abelian sheaf of $c^*N$: the germ $\Gamma(T,c^*N)\to(c^*N)_{\bar s}$ is an isomorphism. Apply the same result to $\mathcal O_T$. Its germ identifies $(\mathcal O_T)_{\bar s}$ with $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=A$. Under this identification the structural stalk map $A=(\mathcal O_Y)_{\bar y}\to(\mathcal O_T)_{\bar s}=A$ is the identity: for each pointed affine neighbourhood it sends its section to exactly its structural image in the defining colimit $A$. The pullback-stalk formula [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-pullback-stalk] now gives $(c^*N)_{\bar s}=N_{\bar y}\otimes_A A\cong N_{\bar y}$. Invert the germ isomorphism and compose with Step 3. This gives the required $A$-linear isomorphism $N_{\bar y}\to H^q(X_A,F_A)$.

source.place: Tag 08B1 strict-local sections paragraph; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO; sites-modules.tex Tag 05V5.

proof.text: For an affine pointed neighbourhood $U$, use [lem-sc-etale-triple-strict-henselization-identification] on its etale algebra after localizing an affine base chart at $y$. It identifies the strict henselization at its lifted point with $A$, compatibly with the maps from $U$. Thus $T\to U$ is flat by the structural-flat argument of Step 1. Both $U\to Y$ and $T\to U$ are flat, so successive-flat-base-change compatibility in [lem-sfb-space-flat-higher-image-base-change] identifies exchange along $c$ with exchange first to $U$ and then to $T$. Its affine cohomology formula sends $a\otimes1$ to pullback of $a$ along $X_A\to X\times_YU$. The germ maps of Step 4 send a representative to its class in the pointed-neighbourhood colimit. This proves exactly the asserted formula. Affine pointed neighbourhoods compute the stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples]; for a general $U$, restriction to an affine neighbourhood of its marked point gives the same formula by functoriality of pullback. Every component is natural in $F$ and linear over its structure ring, so the resulting isomorphism is natural and $A$-linear.
